metadata.change_summary: Added analytically optimized per-hole "tube" implicit surfaces (per-contact crossing positions) and a bounded monotone local kernel refinement to the existing distance-difference candidate/offset selection. Local exact objective improved from 6.5426 to 6.5225 (baseline initial_level_set: 405.08).
metadata.rationale: Host reinitializes with skfmm.distance, so objective_v1 depends only on the zero isosurface. With 70 sparse labels on 4 vertical drillholes (15 outside, 51 inside, 4 contacts), the sign must flip along each hole between the last outside and first inside label; for any field phi(label) <= |z_label - c|, giving a 1-D per-hole tradeoff in crossing offset p (analytic optimum F=6.5139 at p=[0.269,0.247,0.312,0.247]). A single global offset (previous 6.5426, contact phi=0.25) cannot realize per-hole p, so the solver groups sparse cells by non-axis coordinates, optimizes each hole's p on the analytic label loss plus global contact mean/variance, and blends per-hole planes laterally (sigma 2.5/4/7). Exact objective scoring selects among tube, distance-difference, contact-pinned/soft, smoothed-label, sketch and initial-level-set candidates; then per-contact cylindrical (sigma 6) and 3D Gaussian (sigma 2.5, 5) kernels are tuned by greedy coordinate descent accepting only strict improvements. Validation: public selfcheck passes; exact copper.objective score 6.5225 with 0 label mismatches, contact RMSE 0.271, 12.3 s, deterministic, finite float64 with both signs. The remaining ~0.009 gap to the analytic bound comes from skfmm discretization and far labels whose nearest isosurface is a neighbouring hole, so the instance is essentially at its floor. Failed alternatives preserved in research.md: harmonic Laplace interpolation (all-positive field) and Gaussian label convolution (degenerate zero set).

panel.brief:
Round 1 result: baseline initial_level_set scored loss 405.08 (54 label mismatches, contact RMSE 5.56); new data-driven solver reaches local exact score 6.543 (0 mismatches, contact RMSE 0.25, 31890 positive voxels), a 62x improvement, in ~1 s on the 40x50x30 drillholes_3d case.

Key insight: the host reinitializes any field via skfmm.distance, so objective_v1 depends only on the zero isosurface, not field amplitude. With only 70 labeled cells on 4 vertical holes (15 outside, 51 inside, 4 contacts at (15,27,19),(25,27,15),(35,27,14),(38,21,11)), the robust construction is a signed distance difference: phi = EDT(~outside) - EDT(~inside), positive inside. This Voronoi-like implicit surface already gives loss 6.844 with zero mismatches.

Candidate (digest 3d1f8f7e... parent, initial level set) -> new solver at /workspace/candidates/0/solver.py: builds several candidate fields (plain distance difference; contact-pinned variants adding contacts to both/inside/outside seed sets; Gaussian-smoothed signed label fields sigma 0.75-2; sketch-derived and blended surfaces for 2D; initial level set fallback), scores each with an exact reimplementation of objective_v1 (including the 2D sketch Procrustes formula and per-observation weights) using skfmm.distance, then sweeps a global isosurface offset -1.5..1.5 (step 0.1) for the first six candidates and locally refines the winner with 0.02 steps. Time-guarded at 50% of the wall budget, deterministic, returns contiguous finite float64 with both signs.

Measured alternatives: harmonic Laplace interpolation with the 70 Dirichlet labels produced an all-positive field (invalid); normalized Gaussian convolution of labels at sigma 1-6 produced degenerate/no-negative-sign fields (invalid). Contact-pinned variants and fine offsets explain the improvement from 6.844 to 6.543. The current solver's offset grid strictly contains 0.0 and all previously tested candidates, so it can only match or improve 6.543; finer refinement is safe because the internal score replicates the public objective exactly.

The theoretical floor for this observation set (sum of softplus penalties on cells adjacent to the 4 contacts plus contact mean/variance terms, with contacts also counted as positives) is roughly 5-7, so 6.54 is already near optimal and further gains are small.

Public selfcheck passes (2D/3D fixture admission). Remaining alternatives preserved in /workspace/research.md: per-hole or anisotropic offsets, level-set evolution/coordinate descent on boundary voxels, RBF potential-field interpolation, and per-contact seed weighting. Recommendation for the next branch: keep the distance-difference candidate family and refine sub-voxel interface positioning near the four contacts rather than changing the global model.
